We are NovaX Lab from College Saint Andre, competing in the Kigali NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Be An Earth System Trend Detective!"). We have strong skills in software, coding, and web development to analyze data.

We need members skilled in graphic design, multimedia, or writing to complete our squad. Join us to build an impactful solution!
summary:
AgriNova is a Rwanda-first agricultural decision-support platform developed by Team NovaX Lab for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses a critical problem faced by farmers: making informed crop-rotation decisions under changing rainfall, rising temperatures, water limitations, and declining soil health.

Our web application combines NASA POWER historical climate observations with farmers' local information, including location, crop history, soil type, and agricultural priorities. Farmers can register their farms, explore rainfall and temperature patterns, compare crop-rotation options, and save plans for future growing seasons.

AgriNova also connects agricultural communities through Nova Connect, Nova Market, and the developing Nova Chat messaging system. These features support knowledge sharing and access to buyers and sellers.

Built using JavaScript, Supabase, and Cloudflare, AgriNova transforms complex Earth observation information into accessible farming tools. Rotation scores are illustrative and require further agronomic validation. Our vision is to empower farmers with useful data, stronger connections, and more resilient farming decisions.
details:
AgriNova: Transforming Earth Observations into Smarter Farming Decisions

The Problem

Agriculture is essential to Rwanda's livelihoods and food security. However, farmers face increasingly difficult decisions because of variable rainfall, temperature changes, water shortages, declining soil fertility, and limited access to understandable agricultural information.

Crop rotation is an important strategy for managing soil health, but selecting the appropriate sequence of crops requires considering several factors together: climate, soil conditions, crop characteristics, water availability, and the farmer's priorities.

Many smallholder farmers lack simple tools that bring this information together. Scientific climate datasets are publicly available, yet interpreting them and connecting them to everyday farming decisions can be challenging.

Our Solution

Team NovaX Lab developed AgriNova, a web-based agricultural decision-support platform that combines NASA Earth observation resources with farmer-provided information.

AgriNova helps farmers explore possible crop rotations, understand historical climate conditions, manage their growing seasons, and connect with other agricultural participants.

Our objective is to make science-based agricultural planning more accessible, particularly for farming communities in Rwanda.

How AgriNova Works

1. Farm registration

A farmer signs in using Google authentication and registers a farm, including district, sector, approximate area, soil type, and relevant crop information. Personal farm records are stored through Supabase.

2. NASA climate intelligence

The application provides access to NASA POWER historical rainfall and temperature information for selected locations. This allows farmers to review climate history alongside their own knowledge of local farming conditions.

3. Crop-rotation planning

AgriNova compares illustrative rotation alternatives using educational scoring factors related to soil health, water needs, and crop diversity. Farmers can adjust priorities and explore different possibilities before saving their plans.

4. Farmer collaboration

Nova Connect supports community discussions. Nova Market allows registered users to publish agricultural offers and buyer requests. Nova Chat is being integrated to support private communication between participating farmers.

5. Additional planning tools

The prototype includes an agricultural adviser, a climate what-if simulator, farm mapping, a greenhouse planning section, and a crop photo review interface. Advanced AI features depend on separately configured services.

NASA Data and Scientific Relevance

AgriNova uses NASA POWER as its principal source of historical meteorological information. Historical temperature and precipitation observations provide context for crop-planning decisions.

NASA data is combined with information supplied by farmers rather than presented as a substitute for their local agricultural experience.

NASA POWER provides gridded historical estimates, not measurements taken directly on each farm. Our rotation scores are currently illustrative rather than scientifically calibrated predictions.

Technology Used

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Vite
  • Backend: Supabase PostgreSQL and authentication
  • Hosting: Cloudflare Pages and server-side functions
  • Climate information: NASA POWER API
  • Mapping: OpenStreetMap-based location context
  • Development: GitHub and GitHub Codespaces
  • AI: Rule-based educational assistance, with optional NVIDIA-hosted AI services when configured

Innovation

AgriNova's innovation is not simply displaying climate data. It brings together historical Earth observations, farmer-provided information, crop-rotation comparisons, personal farm records, and agricultural collaboration within one accessible digital platform.

The prototype is designed around Rwanda's 30 districts, with the potential to expand its methods to additional regions using appropriate local data.

Intended Impact

AgriNova aims to help farmers:

  • Understand historical climate conditions.
  • Explore crop-rotation alternatives.
  • Improve agricultural planning and recordkeeping.
  • Share practical farming experiences.
  • Connect with potential buyers and sellers.
  • Make more informed decisions about soil and water management.

Development Status and Next Steps

We have developed a functional web prototype with Google authentication, private farm registration, database-backed records, crop-rotation comparisons, community features, and marketplace functionality.

Private farmer messaging has a configured backend and is undergoing frontend integration and testing.

The next stages include validation with agronomists and farmers, stronger localized crop and soil datasets, improved Kinyarwanda accessibility, broader field testing, and evaluation of the usefulness of rotation recommendations.

Our vision: Make agricultural knowledge, Earth observations, and practical planning tools accessible to farmers who need them most.
